newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ifo - Italy lacks the sustainability needed for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Ifo - Italy lacks the sustainability needed for EMU.

text.p: Italy may hit the Maastricht Treaty reference target on deficit levels required for European economic and monetary union (EMU), but should nevertheless be kept out of the first round of euro nations, Germany's Ifo economic research institute said on Monday.

While Ifo said Italy's deficit is likely to be at 3.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 -- matching the maximum allowed by the treaty -- it said this number would be the result of "creative accounting" and would not reflect the country's readiness to join the euro.
The institute suggested Italy should not be allowed to join EMU at the scheduled launch date in January 1999, but first be made to prove its reliability on fiscal restraint.
"It is likely that the public deficit will not exceed 3.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997," Ifo said in country report on the Italian economy.
"But this achievement is only a formal one and it has to be regarded as far from reliable because of many and significant means of 'creative accounting' and other measures to trim the deficit."
"And sustainability is missing," the report said.
Ifo said Italy would nonetheless meet Maastricht rules on consumer prices and interest rates, and noted that public debt had been reduced somewhat in recent years.
But it said debt levels were still far away from EMU targets with an expected ratio of 123 percent of GDP.
Maastricht calls for debt to reduced to 60 percent of GDP.

Ifo noted Italian government plans to cut the budget deficit to 1.8 percent and debt to 116 percent of GDP by the year 2000. But it said this commitment should be proved before Italy joins the single currency project.

"Considering the fact that the credibility of Italian fiscal policy has suffered significantly over decades, it should be recommended that Italy first has to provide proof of fulfilling the targets of its own convergence programme in a reliable way before it is allowed to join EMU in 2001 or 2002," Ifo said.
